title: On AI, Bernie Is the Last Conservative
author: Gregory Conti
content:
![On AI, Bernie Is the Last
Conservative](https://storage.ghost.io/c/65/af/65afbdb5-30bf-4286-acc4-9535069adb42/content/images/2026/09/AP26052068768355.jpg)

Conservatism might be defined as the preference for the devil you know over
the devil you don't. The conservative wants to protect the social order, even
with all its imperfections, from sudden upheaval. If you approve of a society
taking a proverbial leap in the dark, then whatever else you may be, you are
not a conservative. In the words of Edmund Burke, what the conservative
recoils from above all is "rashly to engage in perilous adventures."

> "Whatever else you may be, you are not a conservative."

Artificial intelligence is the ultimate devil you don't know. The widespread
embrace of it is certainly a "perilous adventure." But almost alone in our
political class, it is not a conservative but America's best-known socialist
who is proposing a pause on AI development and a permanent ban on the
development of artificial superintelligence.

Displaying conservative instincts is not without precedent for Bernie Sanders,
the Vermont senator and political independent who ran for the Democratic
presidential nomination in 2016 and 2020. When he rose to national prominence
a decade ago, he was tolerant of gun ownership and skeptical of mass
immigration. In this way, he resembled an older version of the American left,
which sought a greater slice of the pie for workers but also to protect the
dignity, independence, and way of life of average working people. Where
conservatives believed that important traditions and folkways were endangered
by ideological novelty, cultural revolution, and government overreach, the old
left saw the principal danger as exploitation by corporations and the rich.
But neither conservatives nor social democrats sought to revolutionize their
societies.
